laura: quick summary — ran an apples-to-baseline sweep comparing synthetic traffic vs our replay harness. objective: isolate kernel selection and KV cache interaction on quantized configs. saw a P95 regression only when speculative decoding + kv-cache warmup disabled on l2-13b-8bit. attaching short perf snippet and commands below. anyone seen this pattern? :eyes:

mike: can you paste the perf numbers? which traces? replay or synthetic?

laura: replay first (prod traces sampled), then synthetic with same seq/len distribution. TL;DR: replay P50 ~82ms, P95 ~240ms; synthetic P50 ~78ms, P95 ~190ms for same model+quant. Regression only in replay + speculative enabled.

laura: perf dump (abridged):
```
config,workload,p50_ms,p95_ms,notes
l2-13b-8bit,replay,82,240,speculative=on,kv_warmup=off
l2-13b-8bit,replay,80,195,speculative=off,kv_warmup=off
l2-13b-8bit,synthetic,78,190,speculative=on,kv_warmup=off
```

sanjay: interesting. looks like speculative interacts badly with live replay patterns. could be batching alignment or kernel switch thrash when KV hits are intermittent. did you capture kernel-selection logs?

laura: yep, attached snippet from runtime debug logs: shows frequent kernel change events around the same requests with high latency. gist:
```
[2026-04-01T12:11:23Z] kernel_select: chosen=matmul_fast_v2(seq=32)
[2026-04-01T12:11:23Z] kernel_select: chosen=matmul_smallseq(seq=8)
[2026-04-01T12:11:23Z] kv_cache: miss for req=0x7f, warming=false
[2026-04-01T12:11:24Z] speculative: start decode(token_idx=1)
[2026-04-01T12:11:24Z] kernel_select: rollback -> matmul_fast_v2
```

ashley: hmm. that rollback pattern is suspicious. maybe speculative decoding starts with mini-batches that force alternate kernel path then fallback when KV cache is populated. Could amplify p95 in replay which has more prefix sharing.

mike: what if we force one kernel for the whole request window (disable adaptive kernel switching) as an experiment? is there a cheap flag?

laura: yes, did a quick run with `--kernel-lock=on` in the runtime. result: replay P95 dropped from 240 -> 200ms (speculative on). synthetic unaffected. suggests kernel churn is part of it.

sanjay: good. also try toggling KV warmup (pre-populate prefix caches) in the replay harness to see if warm start removes the regression.

laura: ran that: `replay-harness --warmup-prefixes=10`. result: P95 back to ~185ms even with speculative on and adaptive kernel switching. so two contributors: kernel churn + cold KV.

laura: notes on methodology in case we reproduce:
- sampled 2000 replay requests from production traces (random, same seeds across runs)
- synthetic generator matched seq length distribution, token entropy, and batching pressure
- each config run 10x, median of medians reported
- enabled tracing with `RUNTIME_TRACE=kernel_select,kv_cache,speculative`

ashley: does this change our recommendation for the regression gate? if a model+quant combo shows P95 > threshold only on replay cold starts, maybe gate should require warm-start replay failure too.

mike: I agree. propose we update the regression gate: require 1) replay harness fail AND 2) reproduction with kernel-lock off and warmup off. if both true, escalate. otherwise mark as flaky regression tied to cold KV or heuristic coupling.

laura: drafting a short RFC for the gate change. will attach perf artifacts and raw traces. cc @sanjay for kernel heuristics followup.

ci-bot: loadtest job 1816509999 completed — artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-perf/1816509999/ (10 runs).

sanjay: I'll take the kernel heuristics follow-up. initial hypothesis: add hysteresis to kernel selector (min stable window 50ms) and bias towards seq-optimal kernels on speculative starts. will test on replay harness next week.

ashley: thanks — this is a good triage path. small action items: laura -> RFC + artifacts, sanjay -> kernel hysteresis experiment, mike -> update gate proposal draft.

laura: thanks all. I'll post RFC link once ready. :thumbsup:
